Hi all — following up with a tech-first sketch so Thu's call is focused: 

1) Deployment modes & routing
- For PHI workloads we should use Redwood Private (customer VPC) with mTLS + customer-managed KMS. We'll route requests to the Private control plane and ensure no token leakage to hosted layers.
- Non-PHI inference (sanitized notes or classification only) can go to Redwood Hosted with token auth to save cost. Routing policy: header-based route_key (x-tunica-sensitivity: high|low).

2) SDK setup & auth flow (high level)
- SDKs available: python/js/golang. Recommend server-side SDK in customer infra for PHI path.
- Auth pattern: mTLS handshake + short-lived certs issued through customer KMS; for hosted path we use scoped API keys + per-request signatures.
- We'll provide an SDK example that wraps the KV cache for conversational state; attach sample snippet (see repo link).

3) Embeddings & reranker
- For 1–2M vectors initial index, use our dense vector store with sharded indexes; we recommend 1536-d embeddings (or 768-d quantized variant for cost trade-offs).
- Reranker approach: two-stage — retrieval (FAISS-style) then model-based re-rank with calibrated thresholds. We'll include an eval harness to measure precision/recall on your labeled set.

4) Structured output & tool calling
- We can use schema-constrained JSON outputs (structured output) and tool-calling for deterministic coding suggestions (post-processers).
- We'll version the response schemas and include validation hooks in the SDK so you get early failures during PoC.

Open Qs for Thu's call:
- Do you want the reranker to run synchronously in the inference request path or as an async enrichment? (sync = lower latency SLA, async = cheaper).
- How strict do we want schema validation? Block invalid responses or return with error codes + audit log?

Attachments / links: redwood-prompt-templates-v1.yaml (initial templates), internal SDK snippets repo: https://bitbucket.redwood.internal/repos/tunica-poc/snippets

I'll prepare a short demo notebook to show structured outputs + reranker pipeline.

Thanks —

Hi team — adding the prompt governance / quality angle since Tunica emphasized regulatory sensitivity. A few practical proposals we use with customers: 

- Prompt templates & versioning
  * Keep a template registry (YAML/JSON) with semantic versioning (v1.0.0). Each release must include a test plan and owner. We'll share our initial registry (attached).
  * Tie evals to template versions: stored prompt + test suite -> automated regression alerts.

- Prompt injection & red-team
  * Baseline: input sanitization + context-window partitioning to keep sensitive fields separate.
  * Red-team: simulated adversarial prompts run weekly on a shadow dataset; findings feed changes to templates and prompt pre-processors.
  * For PHI-sensitive flows, add result attestation (signed response hash) and stricter schema enforcement.

- Approval / rollout
  * Canary templates to 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor false-positive metrics, then full rollout.
  * Maintain an approvals ledger (who approved which template/version and why).

I'll bring some concrete examples to Thu's call — sample policy snippets, template repo link, and a short red-team checklist.

Cheers,
Marissa
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
